drug_class: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor (targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Ponatinib is used to treat certain types of leukemia, specifically chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL). It is typically used when other leukemia medicines have stopped working or when your leukemia has a specific mutation called T315I that makes other drugs ineffective. Your doctor prescribes it because it is designed to target the specific cause of your type of leukemia.
how_it_works: Your leukemia is driven by an abnormal protein called BCR-ABL that tells cancer cells to grow out of control. Ponatinib works like a key that fits into and blocks that abnormal protein, essentially turning off the signal that makes cancer cells multiply. By blocking this signal, the drug helps slow or stop the growth of leukemia cells.
common_side_effects: Tiredness or weakness, rash or dry skin, headache, constipation, fever, nausea, joint or muscle pain, swelling in your hands or feet, high blood pressure, and stomach pain are among the most commonly reported side effects.
warnings: This is a very important warning: ponatinib can cause serious and life-threatening blood clots in arteries and veins, which can lead to heart attack, stroke, or damage to other organs. It can also cause serious liver problems, heart failure, and narrowing or blockage of blood vessels throughout the body. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, sudden numbness or weakness, vision changes, difficulty breathing, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 45 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may lower your dose to 15 mg or 30 mg once daily depending on how you respond to treatment or if you experience side effects. Always swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or split it. Take it at the same time each day and never skip or double up on doses.
